chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man forgot to throw the pebbles at the pillars until he arrived in Mecca, he said: He returns and throws them. I said: He missed doing that and left [departed]? He said: There is nothing upon him. I said: What if a man forgot the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa? He said: He repeats the Sa'i. I said: He missed doing that until he left? He said: He returns and repeats the Sa'i, for this is not like throwing the pebbles; indeed, throwing is a Sunnah and the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa is a Faridha (obligatory duty).

key_terms.جِمَار: Pillars (plural of Jamarah) where pebbles are thrown during Hajj
key_terms.سَعْي: Sa'i, the ritual brisk walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.سُنَّة: Sunnah, a recommended or established practice (here used for Ramy)
key_terms.صَفَا: Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.فَرِيضَة: Faridha, an obligatory duty (here used for Sa'i)
key_terms.مَرْوَة: Marwa, the second of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in legal ruling between forgetting to throw pebbles and forgetting to perform Sa'i during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal hierarchy within Hajj rituals by distinguishing between acts of worship that are strictly obligatory (Fard) and those that are recommended (Sunnah). This ruling underscores the principle that neglecting a mandatory pillar like Sa'i between Safa and Marwa requires rectification even after departure, whereas missing the Sunnah act of Ramy al-Jamarat incurs no penalty, reflecting the jurisprudential precedence of Quranic obligations over prophetic traditions.
